summary: Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Rupert Gethin and also studied under Paul Dundas.

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Columbia University. His career includes posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, studied at the University of Tokyo in 1973, and learned under Akira Hirakawa (1971–1974). He was a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2010).

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin (dissertation c. 1937–1940). He held posts at Münster (1950, 1963–1978), Mithila Institute (1954), Bonn (1949, 1955–1963), and Pennsylvania (1971).

Paul Harrison (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Auckland and the Australian National University under supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. His posts include Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford University (from c. 2006).
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at Kanazawa University, attested in 1991 as a lecturer and again in 2002.

Paul Hoswell Hardacre (1915–2010) was a historian who studied at Stanford University (c. 1933–1937) and UCLA (c. 1937–1947). He served on the faculty at Vanderbilt University from c. 1947 to 1980 as a historian of Stuart England.

Paul J. Griffiths (b. 1955) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1983), he held posts at Wisconsin, Chicago, Notre Dame, the University of Illinois Chicago (2000–2007), and Duke University (c. 2007–2017).
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the doctoral supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

Paul Kiparsky (b. 1941) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at MIT under Morris Halle (c. 1963–1965) and King Edward's School, Birmingham, later holding a post at Stanford University from c. 1984.

Paul L. Swanson (b. 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Otani University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD attested 1985), he held posts at Nanzan University and directed the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1999–2009).

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and history. Educated at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University (PhD), he held academic posts at the Free University of Berlin, Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006), and the University of Chicago (c. 1999–2016).

Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. Educated in Paris, he studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EFEO, EPHE, Collège de France (1946), and Yale University (1951).
Paul Nietupski is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Passy (1859–1940) was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure from c. 1881 to 1885. He held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from c. 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) was a French scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. Educated in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes, he held posts at the EFEO (1900) and the Collège de France (1909; 1911–1945).

Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from c. 1870 to 1876. He subsequently held a post at the University of Lyon from c. 1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur (1913–2005) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Rennes and the University of Paris. He held posts at Strasbourg, Paris Nanterre, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Université catholique de Louvain, and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).

Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (1916–1921) and later held positions at Princeton University (c. 1938–1952) and Yale University (1943; 1952–1966).

Paul Thieme (1905–2001) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Göttingen and Berlin. He held posts at Allahabad, Breslau, Halle (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).
